reading.body:
Intuitive Surgical's patent record is mostly surgical hardware, with machine learning appearing at the edges of the portfolio rather than at its center.

The company holds 2,231 granted patents, and the five most recent grants from September 2026 are dominated by instrument mechanics: preloaded instrument interfaces, adjustable jaws, depth-based auto-exposure, and tension control in multi-joint actuation. One of the five, medical procedure video searching using machine learning, is the only entry that names machine learning at all. The portfolio reads as a robotics and instrumentation franchise, not an AI franchise.

That distinction matters for how this company sits in an AI supply chain. Its exposure to the compute and power constraints that bind AI scaling is indirect at most. Surgical robots are deployed in operating rooms, not data centers, and the data does not show any installed base, power draw, or compute footprint that would connect it to that story. The 6,730 installed da Vinci systems cited in the profile are a 2021 figure, and the patent data covers grants since 2001 under the applicant phrase "intuitive surgical," so it captures filings attributed to that name and not necessarily every subsidiary or acquisition.

What the data does not cover is revenue, margins, procedure volumes, or any current installed base. It also does not show whether the machine learning patent reflects a real product line or a single filing. The California law exposure count of 281 is a jurisdiction tally, not a measure of risk.
